A conversation with actors, directors, writers, and special effect makeup artists who found their footing in Hollywood with a horror credit. We explore their stories through sit-down interviews and archival footage of their work. This is not a hosted tour of the genre but an intimate reflection of each subject’s life and career, through a horror focused lens.

02 — Need

Need

The horror genre has been, and continues to be, the frontier of creativity. Its landscape is marked by ingenuity born of budding talent. Its success is apparent across the globe. Timeless classics continue to touch modern audiences on screen with boutique home video releases, commercially successful remakes and archival screenings. Off screen, monolithic characters invade apparel, gaming, and social media.

Horror fans have proven themselves to be voracious when it comes to behind the scenes. Our focus will be to bring fans into the world of the creators and dive into their experiences. We aim to dig into their perspective on the nature of the genre, the mechanics of the style, and give us the juicy, unauthorized stories behind the movies that launched their careers.

03 — Stars

Stars

Careers that began with a horror credit. Actors, a director, a makeup artist. The name came after the credit, or the credit was the name.

  1. 01

    Jamie Lee Curtis

    Halloween (1978)

    Before True Lies, Freaky Friday, and her Academy Award for Everything Everywhere All at Once, Jamie Lee Curtis made her feature debut as Laurie Strode in John Carpenter’s Halloween.

  2. 02

    John Travolta

    Carrie (1976)

    Before Saturday Night Fever, Grease, and Pulp Fiction, John Travolta made one of his first feature appearances as Billy Nolan in Brian De Palma’s Carrie.

  3. 03

    Brooke Shields

    Alice, Sweet Alice (1976)

    Before The Blue Lagoon and Endless Love, Brooke Shields appeared in Alfred Sole’s Alice, Sweet Alice, also released as Communion.

  4. 04

    Matthew McConaughey

    Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation (1994)

    Before Interstellar, and his Academy Award winning role portraying Ron Woodroof in Dallas Buyers Club, Matthew McConaughey starred in Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation.

  5. 05

    Paul Rudd

    Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers (1995)

    Before I Love You, Man and Ant-Man, Paul Rudd played Tommy Doyle in Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers.

  6. 06

    Renée Zellweger

    Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation (1994)

    Before Jerry Maguire, Bridget Jones’s Diary, an Academy Award nomination for Chicago, Cold Mountain, and her Academy Award for Judy, Renée Zellweger starred alongside Matthew McConaughey in Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation.

  7. 07

    Elizabeth Olsen

    Silent House (2011)

    Before Wanda Maximoff, Elizabeth Olsen starred in Silent House.

  8. 08

    Demi Moore

    Parasite (1982)

    Before Ghost, Indecent Proposal, and G.I. Jane, Demi Moore starred in Parasite — Charles Band’s 1982 science-fiction horror film, not the later, unrelated feature of the same name.

  9. 09

    Jason Alexander

    The Burning (1981)

    Before George Costanza on Seinfeld, Jason Alexander appeared in The Burning.

  10. 10

    John Carpenter

    Halloween (1978)

    John Carpenter directed Halloween, The Thing, and They Live, and scored them himself. He returned for Halloween (2018), Halloween Kills, and Halloween Ends as executive producer and composer.

  11. 11

    Bruce Campbell

    The Evil Dead (1981)

    Bruce Campbell played Ash Williams in The Evil Dead, Evil Dead II, and Army of Darkness.

  12. 12

    Tom Savini

    Dawn of the Dead (1978)

    Tom Savini designed the effects for Dawn of the Dead, Friday the 13th, and Creepshow, and played among the creatures he built.

  13. 13

    Johnny Depp

    A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984)

    Before Edward Scissorhands and Pirates of the Caribbean, Johnny Depp made his feature debut as Glen Lantz in A Nightmare on Elm Street.

05 — Form

Form

The subject is what the talent says. The rest of the picture supports that conversation.

This is not built as a host’s tour of the genre, and it is not built on reenactment. The picture is carried by sit-down interviews and by archival material: the films that started these careers, and the careers that followed, in the words of the people who lived both.

  • 01

    Sit-down interviews

    What the talent discusses is the scene. The interview is the record, not a bridge to another format.

  • 02

    Archive in support

    Archival material carries memory, context, and the work itself. It does not replace the person speaking.

  • 03

    The horror credit is the start

    The horror credit is where the story starts. It is not asked to be the whole career, or the whole film.

06 — Comparison

Comparison

The audience for serious horror nonfiction is already on the record. These series, on AMC and on Shudder, are the comparison set in the preliminary packet.

Distinction

Those series showed that viewers will watch for the history, the craft, and the people behind the films. it started with a SCREAMSCREAM asks a narrower question: not only how the films were made, but what the stars remember of the credit that started the career.

  • Eli Roth’s History of Horror

    AMC · Three seasons · 2018–2021

    A hosted survey of the genre’s cycles, subgenres, and the filmmakers who made them.

  • Cursed Films

    Shudder · Two seasons · 2020–2022

    Production histories of films shadowed by accident, tragedy, and the stories that outlived the set.

  • Horror Noire: A History of Black Horror

    Shudder · 2019

    A documentary history of Black horror, told by the artists who shaped it.

  • The Core

    Shudder · Series · 2017

    Mickey Keating’s Shudder series on how fear is built — technique, psychology, and the people in the room. Ten episodes, from 2017.

  • Queer for Fear: The History of Queer Horror

    Shudder · Miniseries · 2022

    A four-part history of queer horror, from the gothic novel to the films that kept that history in plain sight.

  • The 101 Scariest Horror Movie Moments of All Time

    Shudder · Miniseries · 2022

    A clip-driven survey of the moments audiences still cannot shake, argued by people who make and study the genre.
